title: Oversized eCommerce orders: How to deliver them same-day
summary: Oversized eCommerce orders fall between parcel and LTL. See how distributors keep them in checkout with same-day delivery from the branch, no new trucks.
body_markdown:
Oversized eCommerce orders are items[too large or heavy](https://www.curri.com/blog/big-and-bulky-last-mile-delivery) for standard parcel service but too urgent to wait on a freight schedule. Parcel and LTL both do their jobs well. Same-day delivery from the branch covers the orders that land between them, so the buyer can book it right in your checkout.


[Curri for eCommerce](https://www.curri.com/ecommerce) adds that option for big and bulky delivery, the heavy, oversized items a standard parcel truck can't carry. Curri matches each order to a vehicle sized to it, from a car to a flatbed, and dispatches a driver from the branch or store that holds the inventory.


## Which big and bulky orders fall between parcel and LTL?


Parcel suits the box that fits a standard truck, and LTL suits the planned pallet. Oversized eCommerce orders sit in between. They are heavy or awkward enough to test parcel limits, and they are needed too soon for a freight schedule. Water heaters, wire reels and pallets of shingles are the classic examples for[HVAC](https://www.curri.com/industries/hvac) ,[plumbing](https://www.curri.com/industries/plumbing) ,[electrical](https://www.curri.com/industries/electrical) and[building materials](https://www.curri.com/industries/building-materials) distributors.


When a buyer needs one on the jobsite today, an online store with only parcel and freight options has little to offer. The buyer picks up the phone, and a counter that could have been quiet fields another rush call.


Picture a plumbing branch that gets an online order for a 50-gallon water heater at 9 a.m. The contractor's crew needs it to finish an install today. The unit weighs 120 pounds, so parcel adds surcharges or turns it down, and LTL won't arrive until later in the week. The branch ends up booking a driver by phone, one order at a time.


With same-day delivery at checkout, that same buyer sees a delivery window and a price before they pay. The order leaves the branch in a vehicle sized to the unit, and the crew stays on schedule.


The category is large.[Armstrong & Associates and the National Home Delivery Association](https://www.supplychain247.com/article/big-and-bulky-last-mile-market-to-reach-12.34b-in-2027) estimate the U.S. third-party big and bulky last-mile delivery market at about $11.4 billion in 2026, and they project it to reach $12.3 billion in 2027.


## What are oversized parcel surcharges, and what do they add?


Parcel carriers set weight and size limits, and orders that cross them pick up oversize and handling surcharges. The charges stack on top of the base rate, so an oversized order can cost far more to send by parcel than the order itself suggests.


Some items don't get that far. A parcel network can reclass an oversized item or refuse it entirely, which leaves the buyer with nothing to book online. Curri matches the order to a vehicle by weight and dimensions and ships it from the store instead.


## How long does LTL transit time take?


LTL (less-than-truckload) freight moves palletized shipments that don't fill a trailer. It handles heavy orders well and fits planned freight, and Curri offers[LTL](https://www.curri.com/ltl) for exactly that. It runs on a schedule, though.[Major LTL carriers](https://www.fedexfreight.com/en-us/services) typically quote delivery in 1 to 3 days for priority service and 3 to 6 days for economy service, depending on origin and destination.


A contractor who needs material on the jobsite today works on a different clock than a freight schedule. That order calls for a driver and a vehicle that can leave the branch within hours.


For more on the freight side, read the[practical guide to LTL construction delivery](https://www.curri.com/blog/ltl-for-construction-delivery) and how[LTL freight class changes](https://www.curri.com/blog/2025-nmfc-ltl-freight-class-changes) affect pallet shipments.


## How does same-day delivery for heavy items work?


Same-day delivery works because the vehicle fits the load. Curri dispatches from the branch or store that holds the inventory and matches the order to one of 56 vehicle and accessory options, from a car for a small box to a cargo van or Sprinter van for appliances and tall loads, a box truck for pallets, or a flatbed for oversized and long loads.


The buyer stays in your checkout. They see a same-day option, a live price and a delivery window, book it, and follow the driver with live tracking. Photo proof of delivery arrives at the drop. It all runs on the same on-demand network behind[Curri Hotshots](https://www.curri.com/hotshots) .


## What should you check before choosing a delivery method?


A few quick questions point most heavy orders to the method that suits them.


- Does the buyer need it today, or can it wait on a freight schedule?
- Does the item stay inside parcel size and weight limits, or will it pick up surcharges?
- Can the delivery site take the vehicle, whether a van, a box truck or a flatbed?
- Who is on site to receive it, and what proof does the branch need afterward?


Site access is worth checking early. As Curri's[big and bulky guide](https://www.curri.com/blog/big-and-bulky-last-mile-delivery) puts it, treating an oversized load like a slightly larger standard delivery is how loads get turned away at a jobsite that can't accommodate the trailer length. Matching the vehicle to the load and the site up front avoids that.


## Where does same-day fit with your existing carriers?


Keep parcel and LTL for routine and planned orders. They work well when time isn't the deciding factor, and nothing here asks you to change that.


Add same-day for urgent and oversized eCommerce orders. Your checkout then covers every order size, and buyers can get something delivered today without leaving the website.
